nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the bishop's graph on the $n \times m$ board has as vertices the cells $(i, j)$ with $0 \le i < n$ and $0 \le j < m$, and two distinct cells $(i, j)$ and $(i', j')$ are adjacent when they lie on a common diagonal, that is, when $|i - i'| = |j - j'|$.
nodes.title: Bishop's graph

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and $n_1, \dots, n_k \ge 1$, and let $G = P_{n_1} \square \cdots \square P_{n_k}$ be the $k$-dimensional Cartesian grid, the Cartesian product of the paths $P_{n_i}$ on $n_i$ vertices. Then $G$ is almost opposable if and only if at most one of $n_1, \dots, n_k$ is even, and $G$ is opposable if more than one of them is even.
nodes.title: Opposability of Cartesian grids

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and side lengths $n_1, \dots, n_k \in \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-dimensional Cartesian grid has as vertices the tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_k)$ of integers with $0 \le x_i < n_i$ for each $i$, and two tuples are adjacent when they differ in exactly one coordinate, and there by exactly one. It is the Cartesian product $P_{n_1} \square \cdots \square P_{n_k}$ of the paths $P_{n_i}$ on $n_i$ vertices.
nodes.title: Cartesian grid

nodes.summary: For every natural number $N$ there is a tree $T$ on $n \ge N$ vertices such that the second player wins Snort on $T$.
nodes.title: Arbitrarily large trees on which the second player wins Snort

nodes.summary: For a graph $G$, vertices $u$ and $v$ of $G$ and a natural number $n$, the $n$-firework of $G$ at $(u, v)$ is the graph obtained from $G$ by adding $2n$ new vertices, $n$ of which are adjacent only to $u$ and the other $n$ adjacent only to $v$.
nodes.title: Firework of a graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs with vertex sets $V$ and $W$, and let $\varphi$ be a Boolean function of four Boolean arguments. The product $G \varphi H$ is the graph on $V \times W$ in which two distinct vertices $(g_1, h_1)$ and $(g_2, h_2)$ are adjacent exactly when $\varphi(g_1 g_2 \in E(G), h_1 h_2 \in E(H), g_1 = g_2, h_1 = h_2)$ is true.
nodes.title: Graph product given by a Boolean formula

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and $n_1, \dots, n_k \ge 1$. Then the $k$-dimensional strong grid $P_{n_1} \boxtimes \cdots \boxtimes P_{n_k}$, the strong product of the paths $P_{n_i}$ on $n_i$ vertices, is almost opposable.
nodes.title: Almost opposability of strong grids

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs. If $G$ is almost opposable and $H$ has a universal vertex, that is, a vertex adjacent to every other vertex of $H$, then the strong product $G \boxtimes H$ is almost opposable.
nodes.title: Strong products with a graph that has a universal vertex

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ is almost opposable if there are a vertex $u$ and a set $S$ of vertices with $u \in S \subseteq N[u]$, where $N[u]$ is the closed neighbourhood of $u$ ($u$ together with its neighbours), such that the subgraph $G - S$ induced on the vertices outside $S$ is opposable.
nodes.title: Almost opposable graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be compatibly almost opposable graphs. Suppose that for some vertex $u$ of $G$ there are an involutive automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ and an opposition $f$ of the induced subgraph $G - u$ on the vertices other than $u$ such that $\alpha(x) = f(x)$ for every vertex $x \neq u$. Then the Cartesian product $G \square H$ is compatibly almost opposable.
nodes.title: Cartesian products of compatibly almost opposable graphs

nodes.summary: If $G$ and $H$ are compatibly almost opposable graphs, then their strong product $G \boxtimes H$ is compatibly almost opposable.
nodes.title: Strong products of compatibly almost opposable graphs

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ is compatibly almost opposable if there are a vertex $u$, a set $S$ of vertices with $u \in S \subseteq N[u]$ (the closed neighbourhood of $u$), an automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ with $\alpha(\alpha(v)) = v$ for every vertex $v$, and an opposition $f$ of the subgraph $G - S$ induced on the vertices outside $S$, such that $\alpha(x) = f(x)$ for every vertex $x \notin S$.
nodes.title: Compatibly almost opposable graphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $\varphi$ be a Boolean function of four truth values, and let $G \varphi H$ be the formula product, in which distinct pairs $(g_1, h_1)$ and $(g_2, h_2)$ are adjacent when $\varphi$ is true at the atoms $g_1g_2 \in E(G)$, $h_1h_2 \in E(H)$, $g_1 = g_2$, $h_1 = h_2$. Suppose that for all distinct non-adjacent vertices $g_1, g_2$ of $G$ and every vertex $h$ of $H$, $\varphi$ is false at…
nodes.title: Formula products with an opposable first factor

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ is opposable if and only if its complement $\overline{G}$ has an opposition matching.
nodes.title: Oppositions and opposition matchings

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph, let $p$ be a map from its vertices to an index set, with blocks $B_i = \{v : p(v) = i\}$, and let $f$ be a map from the vertices of $G$ to themselves. Suppose that for every index $i$ there is an opposition of the subgraph of $G$ induced on $B_i$ that agrees with $f$ on $B_i$, and that for all vertices $u, w$ with $p(u) \neq p(w)$ we have $uw \in E(G) \iff f(u)f(w) \in E(G)$ and…
nodes.title: Gluing oppositions of blocks

nodes.summary: If $G$ is an opposable graph, then for every graph $H$ the Cartesian product $G \mathbin{\square} H$, the strong product $G \boxtimes H$, and the tensor, lexicographic, co-normal and homomorphic products of $G$ with $H$ are opposable. Here distinct pairs $(g_1, h_1)$ and $(g_2, h_2)$ are adjacent in the tensor product when $g_1g_2 \in E(G)$ and $h_1h_2 \in E(H)$; in the lexicographic product when $g_1g_2 \in E(G)$,…
nodes.title: Standard products with an opposable first factor

nodes.summary: A graph $G$ is opposable if it has an opposition: an automorphism $f$ of $G$ such that for every vertex $v$, $f(f(v)) = v$, $f(v) \neq v$, and $f(v)$ is not adjacent to $v$.
nodes.title: Opposable graphs

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a graph. A subgraph $M$ of $K$ is an opposition matching of $K$ if it is a perfect matching of $K$ and for any two distinct edges $ab$ and $cd$ of $M$, $ac \in E(K) \iff bd \in E(K)$ and $ad \in E(K) \iff bc \in E(K)$.
nodes.title: Opposition matchings

nodes.summary: An opposition of a graph $G$ is an automorphism $f$ of $G$ such that for every vertex $v$, $f(f(v)) = v$, $f(v) \neq v$, and $f(v)$ is not adjacent to $v$; that is, an involutive automorphism moving every vertex outside its closed neighbourhood.
nodes.title: Oppositions

nodes.summary: In Snort on a finite graph $G$, a pair $(u, v)$ of vertices is a response pair if $u \neq v$, $u$ and $v$ are not adjacent (so the first player colouring $u$ and the second answering $v$ is legal), and the first player, now to move, loses from the position in which the first player has coloured $u$ and the second player has coloured $v$.
nodes.title: Snort response pairs

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the king's graph of the $n \times m$ board is the simple graph whose vertices are the pairs $(i, j)$ with $0 \le i < n$ and $0 \le j < m$, in which two distinct pairs $(i, j)$ and $(i', j')$ are adjacent when $|i - i'| \le 1$ and $|j - j'| \le 1$.
nodes.title: King's graph

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the knight's graph of the $n \times m$ board is the simple graph whose vertices are the pairs $(i, j)$ with $0 \le i < n$ and $0 \le j < m$, in which two pairs $(i, j)$ and $(i', j')$ are adjacent when either $|i - i'| = 1$ and $|j - j'| = 2$, or $|i - i'| = 2$ and $|j - j'| = 1$.
nodes.title: Knight's graph

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the queen's graph of the $n \times m$ board is the simple graph whose vertices are the pairs $(i, j)$ with $0 \le i < n$ and $0 \le j < m$, in which two distinct pairs $(i, j)$ and $(i', j')$ are adjacent when $i = i'$, or $j = j'$, or $|i - i'| = |j - j'|$; that is, when they share a row, a column or a diagonal.
nodes.title: Queen's graph

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$, the first player wins Snort on the king's graph of the $n \times m$ board (the Peaceable Kings game).
nodes.title: First player wins Peaceable Kings

nodes.summary: For every finite simple graph $G$ that is almost opposable, the first player wins Snort on $G$.
nodes.title: Almost opposable graphs are first-player wins in Snort

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$ be natural numbers such that $n$ or $m$ is odd. Then the first player wins Snort on the queen's graph of the $n \times m$ board (the Peaceable Queens game).
nodes.title: First player wins Peaceable Queens on boards with an odd side

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. In Snort on $G$ the two players alternately colour a vertex that is not yet coloured and is not adjacent to any vertex coloured by the opponent, and a player with no legal move loses. The first player wins Snort on $G$ when the player who moves first has a winning strategy from the position in which no vertex is coloured.
nodes.title: First player wins Snort

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets of vertices of $G$, the vertices coloured so far by the player to move and by the opponent. A legal move colours a vertex $v$ that lies in neither $A$ nor $B$ and has no neighbour in $B$. With move bound $0$ the player to move loses. With move bound $k + 1$ the player to move wins at $(A, B)$ exactly when some legal…
nodes.title: Snort positions with a move bound

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$, the second player wins Snort on the bishop's graph of the $n \times m$ board (the Peaceable Bishops game) if and only if $n$ or $m$ is even.
nodes.title: Second player wins Peaceable Bishops exactly when a side is even

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $(u, v)$ be a response pair of $G$ whose distance in $G$ is at least $3$ (infinite distance, when $u$ and $v$ lie in different components, is allowed). If the second player wins Snort on $G$, then for every natural number $n$ at least the number $|V(G)|$ of vertices of $G$, the second player wins Snort on the $n$-firework of $G$ at $(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Fireworks preserve second-player wins in Snort

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$, the second player wins Snort on the knight's graph of the $n \times m$ board (the Peaceable Knights game) if and only if $n$ is even or $m$ is even.
nodes.title: Snort on the knight's graph

nodes.summary: If a finite simple graph $G$ is opposable, then the second player wins Snort on $G$.
nodes.title: The second player wins Snort on opposable graphs

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$, the second player wins Snort on the rook's graph of the $n \times m$ board (the Peaceable Rooks game) if and only if $n$ and $m$ are both even.
nodes.title: Snort on the rook's graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. In Snort on $G$, two players alternately colour a vertex of $G$ that is not yet coloured, each with their own colour, and a player may not colour a vertex adjacent to a vertex of the opponent's colour; a player with no legal move loses. The second player wins Snort on $G$ if, starting from the position in which no vertex is coloured, the player who moves first has no winning…
nodes.title: Second-player win in Snort

nodes.summary: The first player wins Snort on the queen's graph of the $2 \times 2$ board (the Peaceable Queens game), and the second player wins Snort on the rook's graph of the $2 \times 2$ board (the Peaceable Rooks game).
nodes.title: Snort on the $2 \times 2$ queen's and rook's graphs

nodes.summary: The first player wins Snort on the complete graph $K_2$, and the second player wins Snort on the graph with two vertices and no edges.
nodes.title: Snort on two vertices

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $n_0, \dots, n_{k-1}$, the $k$-dimensional strong grid $P_{n_0} \boxtimes \cdots \boxtimes P_{n_{k-1}}$ is the simple graph whose vertices are the tuples $(x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ of integers with $0 \le x_i < n_i$ for each $i$, in which two vertices $x$ and $y$ are adjacent if and only if $x \ne y$ and $|x_i - y_i| \le 1$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Strong grid

nodes.summary: For simple graphs $G$ on $V$ and $H$ on $W$, the strong product $G \boxtimes H$ is the simple graph on $V \times W$ in which $(g_1, h_1)$ and $(g_2, h_2)$ are adjacent if and only if $g_1 = g_2$ and $h_1 h_2$ is an edge of $H$, or $g_1 g_2$ is an edge of $G$ and $h_1 = h_2$, or $g_1 g_2$ is an edge of $G$ and $h_1 h_2$ is an edge of $H$.
nodes.title: Strong product of graphs

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
